nodes.summary: For natural numbers $n$ and $m$, an integer polynomial map from $n$ variables to $m$ components is an $m$-tuple $F = (F_0, \dots, F_{m-1})$ of polynomials with integer coefficients in the $n$ variables $x_0, \dots, x_{n-1}$.
nodes.title: Integer polynomial map

nodes.summary: Let $F$ be an integer polynomial map from $n$ variables to $n$ components, let $p$ be a natural number, and let $\bar F \colon (\mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z})^n \to (\mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z})^n$ be the map obtained by reducing the coefficients of $F$ modulo $p$ and evaluating. For a natural number $k$ and $x \in (\mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z})^n$, the $k$-th iterate of $F$ modulo $p$ at $x$ is $\bar F^k(x)$, the result of applying…
nodes.title: Iterates of an integer polynomial map modulo a natural number

nodes.summary: Let $F$ be an integer polynomial map from $n$ variables to $n$ components, viewed as the map $\mathbb{Z}^n \to \mathbb{Z}^n$ given by evaluation. For a natural number $k$ and $x \in \mathbb{Z}^n$, the $k$-th iterate of $F$ at $x$ is $F^k(x)$, the result of applying $F$ to $x$ exactly $k$ times; in particular $F^0(x) = x$.
nodes.title: Iterates of an integer polynomial map

nodes.summary: Let $F = (F_0, \dots, F_{m-1})$ be an integer polynomial map from $n$ variables to $m$ components and let $p$ be a natural number. For $x \in (\mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z})^n$, the value of the reduction of $F$ modulo $p$ at $x$ is $(\bar F_0(x), \dots, \bar F_{m-1}(x)) \in (\mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z})^m$, where $\bar F_i$ is the polynomial obtained from $F_i$ by reducing its coefficients modulo $p$.
nodes.title: Reduction of an integer polynomial map modulo a natural number

nodes.summary: Let $F = (F_0, \dots, F_{m-1})$ be an integer polynomial map from $n$ variables to $m$ components. The value of $F$ at a point $x \in \mathbb{Z}^n$ is the point $(F_0(x), \dots, F_{m-1}(x)) \in \mathbb{Z}^m$.
nodes.title: Evaluation of an integer polynomial map

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
